crow verb

of a rooster

also cock-a-doodle-doo, cockadoodledoo, cock-a-doodle-do

classical

Cic. Div. 2.56: quia gallī victī silēre solērent, canere victōrēs
Traupman 299

canō, canere, cecinī

verb, third conjugation

of a cock, crow

Other words

  • cūcūriō

    also used · late Latin · Traupman 144; Traupman 299

    Found only in the late Carmen dē Philomēlā.

Examples

  • gallō canente spēs redit, aegrīs salūs refunditur

    when the cock crows, hope returns, and health flows back to the sickAmbr. hymn. Aeterne rērum 21–22

See also rooster.

SourcesLewis & Short: cano

John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 144, 299.

Ambrose’s hymn from the Latinitas loci collection (loci-augustinus).
